questions.q: What does a cross filter do that a standard field filter does not?
options: It filters parent records based on whether related records exist
It changes the report format to Matrix
It sorts the results alphabetically
It removes duplicate records
questions.explain: A cross filter looks across a relationship, keeping or excluding parents depending on their related child records.

questions.q: You need accounts that have never had an opportunity. Which cross filter setup is correct?
options: Accounts with Opportunities
Opportunities with Accounts
Accounts without Opportunities
Accounts with or without Cases
questions.explain: "Accounts without Opportunities" returns accounts that have no related opportunity records, an anti-join.

questions.q: A cross filter with WITH is most similar to which SOQL pattern?
options: ORDER BY DESC
GROUP BY ROLLUP
LIMIT 10
WHERE Id IN (SELECT AccountId FROM Opportunity)
questions.explain: WITH is a semi-join, equivalent to IN with a subquery. WITHOUT is the anti-join using NOT IN.

questions.q: What is the purpose of sub-filters on a cross filter?
options: They set the sharing rules for the report folder
They add conditions on the related records, such as Opportunity Amount over 100,000
They choose which chart to show
They rename the secondary object
questions.explain: Sub-filters narrow which related records count. An account qualifies only if it has at least one related record that matches.

questions.q: You add "Accounts with Opportunities" as a cross filter and expect to see opportunity columns. Why might they be missing?
options: Cross filters always hide every column
The report must be saved as tabular first
Cross filters only remove parent records; they do not add child columns
Opportunity columns can only be shown to admins
questions.explain: A cross filter only affects which parent rows appear. To display child fields, use a report type that includes the child object.
